changes.before: Create a `Character` class with a name and health.
changes.after: Give each game character its own health and a shared way to take damage.

before: A class describes how to create objects with related fields and actions. An object created from a class is an instance. Each character instance needs its own name and health. A method is a function defined on the class that instances can use. This lets you reuse the damage calculation while keeping each character's changing health separate.

`class Character` starts a class definition. Its braces contain methods. The constructor is the method run when `new Character(...)` creates an instance. Its parameters receive the supplied values. `this` refers to the instance whose method is running. Assigning `this.health = health` puts the input number into that particular object's health property.

Damage subtracts from the current health. `Math.max(0, difference)` chooses whichever is larger, ensuring health does not fall below zero. This lower bound is inclusive, so zero is permitted. Without the maximum, taking 20 damage from 14 health would produce -6. This rule applies to nonnegative damage amounts as supplied; negative damage would increase health, so a larger application would define and validate its allowed inputs.

The method changes a property and does not return the updated health. Inspect `.health` after calling it. This differs from a pure converter function that returns a new number without editing an object. `const fern` is allowed because the name stays attached to the instance even while its properties change. Constructor and method definitions inside a class omit the function keyword.

Your instances are Luna at 10 and Sol at 8. Damage 3 leaves Luna at 7 while Sol stays at 8. A later large damage amount must leave Luna at zero. Test ordinary subtraction, unchanged second-instance state, and the zero boundary; together these show that methods operate on the right object and obey the chosen health limit.
after:
A class describes how to make a kind of object. Each object made from it is called an instance.

Our `Character` class gives each character a name and health. A method is a function the character can use, such as taking damage.

`class Character` begins the class. Its braces hold the methods.

The `constructor` runs when `new Character(...)` creates a character. Its inputs supply the name and health.

In these method calls, `this` means the character the method is being called on. `this.health = health` saves health on that character.

Subtract the damage from the current health. Then use `Math.max(0, ...)` to choose that result or zero, whichever is larger.

This keeps health from falling below zero. The exercise supplies damage amounts that are zero or greater.

`takeDamage` changes the character's health property. It does not return the new health. Read `.health` after calling it.

`const fern` is allowed because the variable still points to the same character, even when the character's health changes.

Complete `takeDamage(amount)` in the starter. Luna starts with 10 health and loses 3, leaving 7. Sol must stay at 8.

Also check damage larger than the remaining health. It should leave zero.

headings: Keep health at zero or above

project.title: A reusable game character
project.task: Create a class with health and a method for taking damage.
project.done_when: Two characters keep separate health values and health cannot fall below zero.
